newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in active trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Monday for the fifth consecutive session in very active trading, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.06 pct to 103.64
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.05 pct at 102.85
Volume was high at 305 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in the Makam.

"The bond market is becoming very interesting and activity rose sharply today. CPI-linked bonds continue to rally and yields on long bonds are getting close to four percent, which is the lowest level we have seen for years," said one trader.

"The main reason for the rise in inflation-linked bonds is the rise in inflationary expectations. The institutional investors have no other alternative if they want to protect themselves from a rise in inflation," said a trader at Sahar Securities.
Traders noted that the government had not issued CPI-linked bonds for some time, adding supply in the market is very low.
One trader said it remained to be seen if the market was strong enough to continue rising if yields fell below four percent.
"Unlinked bonds were also rising today but on a much slower pace. These bonds are still attractive and they offer yields of 14-14.5 percent," the Sahar trader said.
The Makams rose slightly in mixed trading.

Dollar-linked bonds closed almost unchanged as the dollar rose mildly against the shekel. In the local market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3700 shekels against 3.3690 shekels on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
